newsitem.title: USA: US spot resid prices flat amid softer crude prices.
newsitem.headline: US spot resid prices flat amid softer crude prices.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices finished unchanged Tuesday against Monday's levels in very quiet activity amid softer crude prices.
Domestic fuel oil suppliers have been holding on to their barrels in hopes of pent-up demand unleashing from end-users with the continued strength in the natural gas market, market sources said.
"Basically, we're in a stand-off," a New York trader said.
Despite a sharp pull-back in natural gas futures today, physical gas prices held steady or rose again on forecast of Arctic chill spreading across much of the U.S. this week.

New York Harbor one pct edged stayed in $21.75-22.00 a barrel range, with January paper early talked 25 cents higher at $22.50-23.00 but pegged closer to $22.00-22.50 later with softer crude and a late sell-off in January natgas futures.
High sulphurs in New York were flat, with 2.2 percent pegged still at about $18.50.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour remained in the $23.00 area, traders said.
U.S. Gulf Coast one percent was unchanged at $18.50, while three percent notionally held at $16.00-25.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
New York city gate gas prices firmed 20 cents Tuesday to the $4.60/mmBtu area compared to NYH one percent resid at a $3.47/mmBtu equivalent.
